payload.name: Preserve distinct occurrences in recurring event series
payload.description: When a message describes another occurrence of an event the person has already had (e.g., second, fourth, another win), before updating an existing event memory, check whether it is a distinct dated occurrence; if so, ADD it separately and keep prior memories intact.
content: During extraction from a message that describes a new instance of a recurring event (ordinal 'second', 'fourth', 'another', etc.), do not create an UPDATE or MERGE candidate that would replace an earlier memory of the same event type for the same subject with the new instance; create a separate ADD event candidate for the new instance.

During CRUD, before applying UPDATE/MERGE to an event memory, verify whether the incoming evidence is the same event or a different occurrence. Distinct dates, venues, or ordinal numbers mean distinct events: preserve the old memory, add the new one as a separate event, and keep any previously recorded facts.

If the message explicitly states a cumulative total or ordinal count for the series (e.g., 'that was my fourth'), also store that total as a durable profile/state/event memory so the count can be answered later without re-deriving it from individual events.

solves: Construction agents often convert a later instance of a recurring event (e.g., 'won my fourth tournament') into an UPDATE that overwrites the memory of an earlier instance, destroying evidence needed to infer totals. This rule applies whenever a message describes a subsequent occurrence of an already-recorded repeated event and the agent is editing an existing event memory; it requires keeping each distinct occurrence as its own event and preserving any explicit ordinal or cumulative count. It does not apply to one-off events with no recurring series.
